result.title: SIGNTOK: A Text-Aligned Continuous Pose Tokenizer for Sign Language Generation
result.summary: Text-conditioned sign language generation (SLG) depends not only on the generator but also on the space in which signing is generated. Existing approaches generate directly in pose space, in quantized code spaces, or in learned latent spaces trained for reconstruction. We find that these spaces are organized largely by signer identity rather than linguistic content: on CSL-Daily, a test clip's nearest neighbor in raw pose space is the same sentence signed by another person in only 2% of cases. To address this, we propose SIGNTOK, a continuous pose tokenizer whose latent space is shaped by three training-only heads: a kinematics head that predicts motion dynamics, a sentence-level head that aligns signing with the overall text, and a word-level head that aligns short motion windows with content words. Together, these objectives raise the same-sentence cross-signer nearest-neighbor rate to 82%. On three sign language benchmarks, the same generator trained in the SIGNTOK latent instead of pose space raises back-translation BLEU-4 in five of six benchmark-scorer settings at comparable joint accuracy, and word-level alignment gives higher back-translation scores than sentence-level alignment on every benchmark.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SIGNTOK，一个面向手语生成的连续姿态 tokenizer，用运动学、句级文本对齐和词级对齐三个仅训练期使用的头来塑造潜空间，使其按语言内容而非签名者身份组织，并在三个基准上以回译 BLEU-4 评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文发现原始姿态空间与重建潜空间的最近邻主要由签名者身份而非内容决定，这一「潜空间中内容被无关因素压制」的现象及用训练期辅助头重塑潜表示的线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否被表层因素主导、以及监督目标如何组织潜内容。
